description: Cross-language parity for `Registry.export_schema(module_id, strict)` — the exact envelope pinned by schemas/module-schema-export.schema.json. Four keys, no more. This fixture exists because the three SDKs each emitted a different shape: apcore-python added an always-empty `definitions` (a SchemaDefinition field a descriptor does not have, so `$defs` was already inside input_schema where JSON Schema puts it), apcore-typescript added `name`, `version`, `tags`, `annotations` and `examples` — making its export a partial, non-conforming duplicate of system.manifest.module — and apcore-rust emitted the four correct keys. A polyglot caller reading result['input_schema'] got a value on two SDKs and the right answer by accident on the third.

driver_contract.path: Drive the registry method directly — apcore-python `Registry.export_schema(module_id, strict)`, apcore-typescript `registry.exportSchema(moduleId, strict)`, apcore-rust `Registry::export_schema(name, strict)`. Not the serializing helper, not a profile export: this pins the in-memory envelope.
driver_contract.assertion: Assert the returned object's key set EXACTLY equals the four keys — an extra key is the defect this fixture exists to catch, so a subset check would not catch it. Then assert module_id and description. For strict cases, assert input_schema/output_schema equal the Algorithm A23 conversion (schema_strict_conversion.json pins A23 itself; here only the envelope and the fact that strict reaches both schemas are in scope).
driver_contract.unregistered: An unregistered module_id returns the language's empty value — Python None, TypeScript null, Rust Option::None — never a partially-filled envelope and never a raised error.

test_cases.description: name / version / tags / annotations / examples belong to system.manifest.module. A module declaring all of them still exports exactly four keys.
A schema using $defs keeps them where JSON Schema puts them. There is deliberately no sibling `definitions` key — it was always empty on this path and gave callers a second place to look.
strict=true applies Algorithm A23 to input_schema AND output_schema, and does not change the key set.
None / null / Option::None — never a partially-filled envelope, never a raised error.
